messages:
amina_csm: FYI — Boreal Data reached out asking to onboard a tiny domain adapter they trained (around 350M params) into Redwood Private. They want PHI-safe handling and HSM keywrap for model weights. Timeline: pilot in 3 weeks. Can we scope?

amina_csm: Key asks from customer: private VPC deploy, FIPS-compatible KMS/HSM, quantized 4-bit variant to save cost, and safety/evals for PHI leakage. They also want sample eval prompts and a brief SOC-style checklist.

@toby_eng: Sounds doable but need infra details. Is their adapter a LoRA-style diff or a full merged checkpoint? Also what's the base model?

amina_csm: They said it's an adapter (LoRA) against a Llama2-13b-ish base. They can share a sample merged checkpoint if needed.

vera_ml: For safety: we'll need prompt/response evals (200 pairs), membership inference checks, and some red-team prompts for PHI extraction. Do they have labeled PHI examples or synthetic variants?

amina_csm: They're willing to provide de-identified examples + a small set of synthetic PHI probes. Requested we run our in-house PHI leakage eval and provide a short risk summary.

@toby_eng: Technical constraints: Private deploy supports quantized 4-bit for compatible models, but adapters on top can complicate kernel fusion. If they give the merged checkpoint we can run an automated compatibility check (quick convert test). If it's LoRA-only, we may require merge step during deployment. Any HSM specifics?

jen_ops: HSM/KMS: we support customer-managed keys via our KMS integration for Private. For HSM keywrap we need customer to provide endpoint + certs; ops team will run an on-prem handshake test. SLA wise +3 days to provision after creds.

amina_csm: Customer asked for a simple one-pager checklist for their compliance team and an estimate of cost delta for 4-bit + adapter vs full 13b.

vera_ml: For evals I propose this plan: (1) 200 in-domain QA pairs, (2) 50 worst-case PHI probes, (3) 500 general safety prompts. We'll run: membership inference, token likelihood sniffing, and prefix-reconstruction tests. Deliverable: pass/fail flags + short remediation steps.

@toby_eng: Action items for eng: 1) request merged checkpoint sample from Boreal, 2) run compatibility & quantize test (logs + minimal perf numbers), 3) note if adapter merge required in deployment flow. I can start as soon as the sample is available. ETA 4 business days after sample.

amina_csm: I'll ask Boreal to upload a sample to our secure intake bucket and share a pointer. Tagging @toby_eng and @vera_ml in the ask.

ops-bot: Ticket created: CS-4921 — Boreal Data adapter private onboarding. Assignees: toby_eng, vera_ml, jen_ops. Link: https://redwood.atlassian.example/browse/CS-4921

toby_eng: Quick note — if they insist on HSM-wrapped model weights in the image, we need a small design discussion. HSM-wrapped blobs are fine for key management, but runtime must be able to unwrap in the Private VPC using customer HSM. That adds ~1-2 days to validation.

amina_csm: Noted. I'll surface that to the customer and confirm whether they require runtime-wrapped weights or just KMS for telemetry/encryption at rest.

vera_ml: Also: please request their eval acceptance criteria. E.g., "no PHI hallucination > 0.1% on probes" or similar. We can't promise zero.

amina_csm: Good call. I'll confirm SLOs and return with their acceptance thresholds.

jen_ops: Heads-up: if they want canary rollout + A/B with fallback to hosted model for safety, ops can set routing policy. That helps rollback if any safety regression shows up during pilot.

amina_csm: Excellent — I'll propose that as an option.

toby_eng: OK. Next steps summarized: Amina to get sample & acceptance criteria; ops to prepare HSM onboarding doc; eng to queue compatibility tests once sample is in intake; ML to prepare eval plan.

amina_csm: Thanks all — I'll update the ticket and ping when sample is uploaded. :thumbsup: 

ops-bot: Reminder set for CS-4921: due in 21 days.
